task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: How to define suppression-conditional recommended mix from defensive matchup data
Measuring adherence to a dynamic play-type mix
Causal link from adherence to winning at game or series level
Sample size adequacy with 54 playoff series
Confounding by opponent strength, game states, and overall team quality
Measurement reliability of defensive suppression from play-by-play
Endogeneity of recommended mix and adherence
Multiple testing across play types and thresholds

historical_evidence.finding: Holdout games where a team's play-type mix is closer to the model's recommended mix score more efficiently (strength-controlled gap +3.27 ORtg). Model regret is non-negative by construction.

Possessions on the engine's recommended play type do not score more than other PTs within the series beyond inherent PT PPP; strictest FE test gamma +0.0088, p=0.71. A/B tests explained by engine picking high-PPP play types.
Teams' observed play-type mix in early playoff games only partially matches the model's recommended opener; 4 of 8 sides best matched opener #3, not rank-1. No outcome comparison.
LangGraph agent V5 did not significantly outperform deterministic V4; Holm p=0.062, McNemar p=0.118 on n=40 pairs, override hit 25% on 8 overrides. Sample too small to decide.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Possession-level test of whether the engine's recommended play type yields higher PPP in a series
failed_approaches.why: Null after two-way FE; engine merely selects generally efficient play types, no incremental value detected.
Single-game horizon, no outcome comparison, CUT/PNR muted for tagger floor; cannot assess link to winning.
N=40, insufficient power, multiple testing; unable to isolate suppression-conditional mix value.

evidence_establishes: Alignment with the model's recommended play-type mix correlates with higher offensive efficiency after controlling for team strength (SF-[prior work]).
The engine's play-type recommendation at the possession level does not improve points per possession beyond the inherent efficiency of those play types (SF-[prior work]).
Execution conformance to recommended mixes is imperfect even in key playoff games (SF-[prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix causes or independently predicts winning.
That the efficiency advantage in SF-[prior work] is due to suppression-conditional advice rather than general quality of the mix or team execution.
Any direct link between adherence and series or game outcomes beyond what is already captured by team strength and opponent quality.
own_inferences: The possession-level null suggests that the engine's recommendations lack an incremental causal effect, so adherence to those recommendations is unlikely to have a direct effect on winning beyond what team quality and standard play-type efficiency can explain.

Any observed association between adherence and winning in an observational study would be heavily confounded by overall team ability, coaching, and game situation, making causal interpretation impossible without strong quasi-experimental designs (which the historical evidence suggests are not feasible with the current engine).

The question as posed implies a causal or predictive link; given prior null on the core mechanism, testing for a predictive link is likely to produce an artifact (confounding) rather than a genuine signal.
uncertainties: Whether suppression-conditional recommended mixes can be defined reliably from the available defensive matchup and play-by-play data.
How much variation in adherence exists across games and series in the available data.
Whether winning (a low-frequency binary outcome in playoff series) can be predicted with enough power even after pooling regular season games.
The degree to which the engine's suppression-conditional component is working as intended, given the null at possession level.

historical_effect.explanation: Without historical evidence one might assume that adherence to a sophisticated suppression-conditional mix could be tested for its predictive power on winning. The retrieval revealed a supported association with efficiency but a strong null at the possession level for the engine's recommendations, indicating no incremental value. This shifts the assessment from 'uncertain, maybe testable' to 'likely artifact/untestable due to lack of causal mechanism', leading to a do_not_proceed decision.

blocking_constraints.text: Adherence is confounded with overall team quality, coaching, opponent strength, and game context; without a credible identification strategy the predictive association is uninterpretable.
Only 54 playoff series available as natural units; expanding to game-level regular season still faces low signal-to-noise for winning due to many other determinants.
Defensive suppression states are inferred from matchup and play-by-play data; error in classifying suppression conditions would attenuate any signal and increase risk of artifact.

prior_work.summary: SF-[prior work] shows that general mix alignment correlates with efficiency, but SF-[prior work] shows the engine's play-type recommendations add no incremental PPP value. Together they suggest the engine's recommendations may not capture suppression-conditional value, so testing whether adherence predicts winning is likely to recover only confounding.

risks.text: Team strength, coaching quality, and opponent defensive style confound the adherence–winning relationship.
54 series insufficient to detect a unique effect of adherence on series win/loss; game-level expansion introduces many confounders without sufficient statistical power for a rare outcome.
Suppression-conditional mix definitions may be noisy, reducing power and amplifying RTM_SELECTION.
Defining adherence thresholds, suppression states, and multiple play-type aggregates creates a large multiplicity problem.
Teams with high adherence may be those that are already performing well, leading to regression-to-the-mean artifacts when predicting future winning.

design.estimand: The marginal predictive effect of adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended play-type mix on game win/loss, net of pre-game win probability and team strength.
design.sample: All NBA games from 2022-23 through 2025-26 where a suppression-conditional recommended mix can be computed and adherence measured; expected >3000 games.
design.power: With ~3000 games and a binary outcome, minimum detectable effect for a standardized adherence variable is small (Cohen's d ~0.1) but confounders will reduce effective power; the greatest threat is bias, not sampling error.
design.controls: Pre-game win probability (e.g., from betting markets), team offensive/defensive rating over prior 20 games, home/away, days rest, key injuries (indicator). Also include opponent fixed effects.
design.falsification: Test whether adherence predicts loss against much stronger opponents (the sign should reverse or be null if it merely reflects team quality). Test with placebo recommended mixes (random shuffles or opponent-generic best-practice mix) to see if 'suppression-conditional' label adds value.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register a single continuous adherence metric (e.g., L1 distance between observed and recommended mix, normalized) and one logistic regression specification. All other analyses labeled exploratory.
design.decision_rule: One-sided Wald test that the adherence coefficient is negative (i.e., more adherence -> higher win probability) after controls, with pre-registered alpha 0.05. If placebo tests fail, the study is inconclusive regardless of p-value.
design.data_version: Data frozen as of 2026-06-16, including regular seasons 2022-23 through 2025-26 and playoffs of those seasons.
